sentences.text: Katepensaurus is unique among sauropods for having an additional set of pneumatic openings called laterodiapophyseal fenestrae, which are distinctive openings in the dorsal vertebrae.
The animal also possesses a unique pair of vertebral laminae not seen in any other rebbachisaurid.
The genus name Katepensaurus comes from the Tehuelche word for 'hole', referring to those distinctive openings in the dorsal vertebrae.
The individual represented by the holotype was at least seven years old and still growing when it died.
The genus Katepensaurus contains only one known species, Katepensaurus goicoecheai, based on the partial skeleton UNPSJB-PV 1007.
Katepensaurus was described as a new genus and species in 2013 by Lucio M. Ibiricu, Gabriel A. Casal, Rubén Dario Martínez, Matthew C. Lamanna, Marcelo Luna, and Leonardo Salgado.
The species name goicoecheai honors Alejandro Goicoechea, the owner of the ranch where the fossils were found.
Katepensaurus is classified within the family Rebbachisauridae.
The animal is placed in the subfamily Limaysaurinae, a group of diplodocoid rebbachisaurids.
Katepensaurus shows a mix of traits found in both nigersaurines/rebbachisaurines and limaysaurines.
Katepensaurus lived during the Late Cretaceous in south-central Chubut Province, central Patagonia, Argentina.
The fossil-bearing Lower Member of the Bajo Barreal Formation dates to the Cenomanian or Turonian stages of the early Late Cretaceous, spanning from 100.5 to 89.8 million years ago.
It is debated whether Katepensaurus belongs to the limaysaurines or is a basal rebbachisaurid, as different studies have produced conflicting results.
